'''Isaac Michael Ross''' is a Distinguished Professor and Program Director of Control and Optimization at the [[Naval Postgraduate School]] in Monterey, CA.  He has published a highly-regarded textbook on optimal control theory<ref name="ross:text">I. M. Ross, ''[https://www.amazon.com/Primer-Pontryagins-Principle-Optimal-Control/dp/0984357114 A Primer on Pontryagin’s Principle in Optimal Control],'' Second Edition, Collegiate Publishers, San Francisco, CA, 2015.</ref> and seminal papers in [[pseudospectral optimal control]] theory,<ref name="ross:POC-1">{{cite journal | last1=Michael Ross | first1=I. | last2=Fahroo | first2=Fariba | title=A Pseudospectral Transformation of the Convectors of Optimal Control Systems | journal=IFAC Proceedings Volumes | date=2001 | volume=34 | issue=13 | pages=543–548 | doi=10.1016/S1474-6670(17)39048-1 }}</ref> energy-sink theory,<ref name ="ross:ES-1">{{cite journal | last1 = Ross | first1 = I. M. | year = 1996 | title = Formulation of Stability Conditions for Systems Containing Driven Rotors | journal = Journal of Guidance, Control and Dynamics | volume = 19 | issue = 2| pages = 305–308 | doi=10.2514/3.21619| bibcode = 1996JGCD...19..305R | hdl = 10945/30326 | s2cid = 121987998 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> the [[Asteroid impact avoidance|optimization and deflection of near-Earth asteroids and comets]],<ref name="ross:NEA-1">{{cite journal | last1 = Ross | first1 = I. M. | last2 = Park | first2 = S. Y. | last3 = Porter | first3 = S. ==Theoretical contributions==
Although Ross has made contributions to energy-sink theory, [[attitude dynamics and control]]<ref name="ross:acs-rb">{{cite journal | last1 = Fleming | first1 = A. | last2 = Sekhavat | first2 = P. | last3 = Ross | first3 = I. M. | year = 2010 | title = Minimum-Time Reorientation of a Rigid Body | journal = Journal of Guidance, Control and Dynamics | volume = 33 | issue = 1| pages = 160–170 | doi=10.2514/1.43549| bibcode = 2010JGCD...33..160F | s2cid = 120117410 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ross |first=I. Michael |date=2003-07-01 |title=Linearized Dynamic Equations for Spacecraft Subject to J2 Perturbations |url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/10.2514/2.5095 |journal=Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics |volume=26 |issue=4 |pages=657–659 |doi=10.2514/2.5095|bibcode=2003JGCD...26..657R |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ross |first=I. Michael |date=2002-07-01 |title=Mechanism for Precision Orbit Control with Applications to Formation Keeping |url=https://arc.aiaa.org/doi/10.2514/2.4951 |journal=Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics |volume=25 |issue=4 |pages=818–820 |doi=10.2514/2.4951|bibcode=2002JGCD...25..818R |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Asteroid impact avoidance|planetary defense]],<ref name="ross:NEA-2">{{cite journal | last1 = Park | first1 = S. Y. | last2 = Ross | first2 = I. M. | year = 1999 | title = Two-Body Optimization for Deflecting Earth-Crossing Asteroids | journal = Journal of Guidance, Control and Dynamics | volume = 22 | issue = 3| pages = 415–420 | doi=10.2514/2.4413| bibcode = 1999JGCD...22..415P }}</ref>  he is best known<ref name="mor-2005"/><ref name ="kang-2010"/><ref name="li-2011"/><ref name="res-2008"/><ref name="pw-2004">{{cite journal | last1=Williams | first1=Paul | title=Application of Pseudospectral Methods for Receding Horizon Control | journal=Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics | date=2004 | volume=27 | issue=2 | pages=310–314 | doi=10.2514/1.5118 | bibcode=2004JGCD...27..310W }}</ref> for work on [[pseudospectral optimal control]].<ref name="ross:POC-4">{{cite book | last1=Ross | first1=M.I. | last2=Fahroo | first2=F. | title=Proceedings of the 2004 American Control Conference | chapter=Discrete verification of necessary conditions for switched nonlinear optimal control systems | date=2004 | pages=1610–1615 vol.2 | doi=10.23919/ACC.2004.1386807 | isbn=0-7803-8335-4 }}</ref><ref name="ross:POC-2">{{cite book | last1=Ross | first1=I. Michael | last2=Fahroo | first2=Fariba | title=New Trends in Nonlinear Dynamics and Control and their Applications | chapter=Legendre Pseudospectral Approximations of Optimal Control Problems | series=Lecture Notes in Control and Information Sciences | date=2004 | volume=295 | pages=327–342 | doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45056-6_21 | isbn=978-3-540-40474-3 }}</ref><ref name="ross:POC-3">{{cite journal | last1 = Ross | first1 = I. M. | last2 = Fahroo | first2 = F. | year = 2004 | title = Pseudospectral Knotting Methods for Solving Optimal Control Problems | url = https://zenodo.org/record/1235937| journal = Journal of Guidance, Control and Dynamics | volume = 27 | issue = 3| page = 3 | doi=10.2514/1.3426}}</ref><ref name="ross:POC-5">{{cite journal | last1 = Ross | first1 = I. M. | last2 = Fahroo | first2 = F. | year = 2004 | title = Pseudospectral Methods for the Optimal Motion Planning of Differentially Flat Systems | url = https://zenodo.org/record/1265714| journal = IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control | volume = 49 | issue = 8| pages = 1410–1413 | doi=10.1109/tac.2004.832972| bibcode = 2004ITAC...49.1410R | hdl = 10945/29675 | s2cid = 7106469 | hdl-access = free }}</ref> In 2001, Ross and Fahroo announced<ref name="ross:POC-1"/>  the [[covector mapping principle]], first, as a special result in [[pseudospectral optimal control]], and later<ref name="ross:POC-4"/>  as a general result in [[optimal control]].  This principle was based on the [[Ross–Fahroo lemma]] which proves<ref name ="kang-2010"/> that dualization and [[discretization]] are not necessarily [[commutative operation]]s  and that certain steps must be taken to promote commutation.  When [[discretization]] is commutative with dualization, then, under appropriate conditions, [[Pontryagin's minimum principle]] emerges as a consequence of the [[rate of convergence|convergence of the discretization]].  
Together with [[Fariba Fahroo|F. Fahroo]], W. Kang and Q. Gong, Ross proved a series of results on the convergence of pseudospectral discretizations of optimal control problems.<ref name="converge:summ">{{cite book | last1=Kang | first1=Wei | last2=Ross | first2=I. Michael | last3=Gong | first3=Qi | title=Analysis and Design of Nonlinear Control Systems | chapter=Pseudospectral Optimal Control and Its Convergence Theorems | date=2008 | pages=109–124 | doi=10.1007/978-3-540-74358-3_8 | isbn=978-3-540-74357-6 }}</ref>  Ross and his coworkers showed that the [[Legendre pseudospectral method|Legendre]] and [[Chebyshev pseudospectral method|Chebyshev]] pseudospectral discretizations converge to an optimal solution of a problem under the mild condition of boundedness of variations.<ref name="converge:summ"/>

==Software contributions==
In 2001, Ross created [[DIDO (optimal control)|DIDO]], a software package for solving [[optimal control]] problems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Conway|first=Bruce A.|date=2011-09-15|title=A Survey of Methods Available for the Numerical Optimization of Continuous Dynamic Systems|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/s10957-011-9918-z|journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications|volume=152|issue=2|pages=271–306|doi=10.1007/s10957-011-9918-z|s2cid=10469414|issn=0022-3239|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>B. Honegger, "NPS Professor's Software Breakthrough Allows Zero-Propellant Maneuvers in Space." Navy.mil. United States Navy. April 20, 2007. (Sept. 11, 2011) http://www.elissarglobal.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/Navy_News.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030610/http://www.elissarglobal.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/Navy_News.pdf |date=2016-03-04 }}.</ref><ref>{{Cite arXiv|eprint=2004.13112|class=math.OC|first=Isaac|last=Ross|title=Enhancements to the DIDO Optimal Control Toolbox|year=2020}}</ref> Powered by [[Ross–Fahroo pseudospectral method|pseudospectral methods]], Ross created a user-friendly set of objects that required no knowledge of his theory to run DIDO.  This work was used in on pseudospectral methods for solving optimal control problems.<ref name="GongCo">{{cite book | last6=Bollino | first6=Kevin | last3=Bedrossian | first3=Nazareth S. | last4=Fahroo | first4=Fariba | last5=Pooya Sekhavat | last2=Wei Kang | last1=Qi Gong | title=2007 46th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control | chapter=Pseudospectral Optimal Control for Military and Industrial Applications | date=2007 | pages=4128–4142 | doi=10.1109/CDC.2007.4435052 | isbn=978-1-4244-1497-0 }}</ref>  DIDO is used for solving optimal control problems in aerospace applications,<ref name="hawkins-mit">A. M. Hawkins, ''Constrained Trajectory Optimization of a Soft Lunar Landing From a Parking Orbit,'' S.M. Thesis, Dept. of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, 2005. http://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/32431
</ref><ref name="rea-mit">J. R. Rea, ''A Legendre Pseudospectral Method for Rapid Optimization of Launch Vehicle Trajectories,'' S.M. Thesis, Dept. of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, 2001. http://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/8608
</ref> search theory,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Optimal Search for Moving Targets|last1=Stone|first1=Lawrence|last2=Royset|first2=Johannes|last3=Washburn|first3=Alan|publisher=Springer|year=2016|isbn=978-3-319-26897-2|location=Switzerland|pages=155–188}}</ref> and [[robotics]].  Ross' constructs have been licensed to other software products, and have been used by [[NASA]] to solve flight-critical problems on the [[International Space Station]].<ref name="SIAMp1">W. Kang and N. Bedrossian, "Pseudospectral Optimal Control Theory Makes Debut Flight", ''[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] News'', Vol. 40, Page 1, 2007.</ref>

==Flight contributions==
In 2006, NASA used [[DIDO (optimal control)|DIDO]] to implement zero propellant maneuvering<ref>[http://www.nasa.gov/mission_pages/station/research/experiments/274.html "International Space Station Zero-Propellant Maneuver (ZPM) Demonstration (ZPM) - 07.29.14"]. NASA.</ref> of the [[International Space Station]]. In 2007, ''[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] News'' printed a page 1 article<ref name="SIAMp1" /> announcing the use of Ross' theory.  This led other researchers<ref name="GongCo" />  to explore the mathematics of [[pseudospectral optimal control]] theory.  DIDO is also used to maneuver the Space Station and operate various ground and flight equipment to incorporate [[autonomy]] and performance efficiency for [[nonlinear control system]]s.<ref name="RK">{{cite journal | last1 = Ross | first1 = I. M. | last2 = Karpenko | first2 = M. | year = 2012 | title = A Review of Pseudospectral Optimal Control: From Theory to Flight | journal = Annual Reviews in Control | volume = 36 | issue = 2| pages = 182–197 | doi=10.1016/j.arcontrol.2012.09.002}}</ref>

==Awards and distinctions==
In 2010, Ross was elected a Fellow of the [[American Astronautical Society]] for "his pioneering contributions to the theory, software and flight demonstration of [[pseudospectral optimal control]]."  He also received (jointly with [[Fariba Fahroo]]), the [[AIAA]] Mechanics and Control of Flight Award for "fundamentally changing the landscape of flight mechanics".   His research has made headlines in ''SIAM News'',<ref name="SIAMp1" />  ''[[IEEE]] Control Systems Magazine'',<ref name="IEEECoverStory">N. S. Bedrossian, S. Bhatt, W. Kang, and I. M. Ross, Zero-Propellant Maneuver Guidance, ''IEEE Control Systems Magazine'', October 2009 (Feature Article), pp 53–73.</ref> ''[[IEEE Spectrum]]'',<ref name="IEEESpectrum-2012"/> and ''Space Daily''.<ref name="SDnews">TRACE Spacecraft's New Slewing Procedure, ''Space Daily'', December 28, 2010</ref>
